intended_object: The diagonal torus action on the A-points A ⊗_ℤ L_ℤ of the Chevalley (adjoint) lattice of a split semisimple Lie algebra over ℚ. A parameter s : Φ ∪ {0} → Aˣ scales each weight-basis vector b_i by the character value ∏_α s_α^{⟨μ_i, α^∨⟩}, i.e. the product of the coroot cocharacters. Inferred from the docstring, the name and the module context.
explanation: The body specialises the library's general construction `kostantTorusPoints` (= `basisWeightTorus (b.baseChange A) wt`, i.e. `basisDiagonal` with the characters `torusCharacter s (wt i)`, moved into `GeneralLinearGroup`) to the Chevalley weight basis `chevalleyWeightBasisFin`. Its weights `chevalleyWeightFin` are the integer coroot eigenvalues of the basis vectors (`isCartanWeightVector_chevalleyWeightBasisFin`). So a point s scales each base-changed basis vector b_i by ∏_α s_α^{wt i α}, which is exactly what the docstring describes. The docstring is explicit about the degenerate case: the parameter is indexed by all weights, the zero weight has a vanishing coroot and so acts trivially. It also says the image is not claimed to be the maximal torus of a pinning, so the definition promises no more than it delivers. This is a specific object, the torus action for the Chevalley lattice. The value ring A is already arbitrary, and the general version (any lattice with a weight basis) exists in the library as `kostantTorusPoints`. The ℚ, Killing-form and Cartan-subalgebra hypotheses are what the Chevalley lattice and its weight basis need. I did not search Mathlib; to my knowledge it has no counterpart for the Chevalley lattice or a torus acting on it.
